named_confounds: genre composition (the late period has more juvenile works, which have a higher base rate)
few early works (752 before 1876 vs 6014 from 1876 on), and the earliest decades are sparse
date uncertainty (about half the works have low or medium date confidence)
annotation/coding drift in the domain labels
one passage per work, so each work's rate is a single 0/1 value
rationale: Method: there are 6766 works and every one has exactly one passage, so a work's rate is 0 or 1 (does the passage carry the DISTANCE_TRAVEL label or not). Works dated 1876 or later count as late. Within each genre I averaged the work rates for early and late, took late minus early, then averaged that difference equally across the 8 genres. The effect is +0.052 passages per passage. A bootstrap that resamples works within each genre-by-period cell (2000 draws) gives a 95% CI of [0.033, 0.069]. The late rate is higher than the early rate in all 8 genres, with differences between about +0.04 and +0.06. Artifact checks: the share of early vs late works by origin and by date confidence is similar in both periods. Mean n_editions (1.09 vs 1.08) and author productivity (19.5 vs 21.1 works per author) barely differ. Genre mix does shift toward juvenile in the late period, but the estimate is already stratified by genre. A weighted regression adjusting for genre, origin, date confidence, log editions and log author productivity, with standard errors clustered by author, gives +0.051 [0.032, 0.071]. The effect holds within each date-confidence level: high 0.044 (bootstrap CI [0.011, 0.073]), medium 0.070, low 0.044. It also holds within each origin: UK 0.029, US 0.068, unknown 0.054. Treating year as continuous with genre fixed effects gives a positive slope (p about 1e-5). By decade, the rate is about 0.05 for 1850-1870 and rises to about 0.10-0.13 from the 1880s on, which fits a real change around the cutoff. Caveats: the early sample is small, and the 1840s value of 0.15 rests on only 73 works. The corpus is a sample and may not represent everything published. The labels come from coding and could have drifted over time. The cited passages are late, well-dated works that carry the DISTANCE_TRAVEL label. They only illustrate the construct and do not by themselves establish the trend. Reasoning uses only the supplied data.
